# Signed notes with the verdict of two rule sets: this package (ParsePayload)
# and the verifier (kingres-verify: signednote.Parse, then checkpoint.Parse of
# the text). One case per line, four fields separated by a tab:
#
#   name  anchor  verifier  note
#
# anchor and verifier are "accept" or "refuse"; note is a Go double-quoted
# string. Where the two verdicts differ, the case is one of the two places where
# this package is stricter on purpose (the byte 0x7f, DEL, anywhere in the note;
# a note over 16 KiB, which is tested separately) and the name says so.
# TestPayloadCorpus holds ParsePayload to the anchor column. This file has a
# byte-identical copy in the verifier module
# (verifier/internal/checkpoint/testdata/payload_corpus.txt), and a test there
# holds the verifier's real parsers to the verifier column; a test of this
# package fails when the two copies differ (correction 92 and 97). Change both
# together.

good	accept	accept	"kingres.example/agg\n17\ncnJycnJycnJycnJycnJycnJycnJycnJycnJycnJycnI=\n\n\u2014 kingres.example/agg AAAAAA==\n"
two-keys-same-name-other-id	accept	accept	"kingres.example/agg\n17\ncnJycnJycnJycnJycnJycnJycnJycnJycnJycnJycnI=\n\n\u2014 kingres.example/agg AAAAAA==\n\u2014 kingres.example/agg AAAAAQ==\n"
two-keys-other-name	accept	accept	"kingres.example/agg\n17\ncnJycnJycnJycnJycnJycnJycnJycnJycnJycnJycnI=\n\n\u2014 kingres.example/agg AAAAAA==\n\u2014 witness.example/w AAAAAA==\n"
one-extension-line	accept	accept	"kingres.example/agg\n17\ncnJycnJycnJycnJycnJycnJycnJycnJycnJycnJycnI=\nsome extension\n\n\u2014 kingres.example/agg AAAAAA==\n"
